subject: Recap: GPU reservation qualification and proposed pathways
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Lydia Cho <lydia@medsprint.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: GPU reservation qualification and proposed pathways

Lydia — thanks again for carving out time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared picture and clear next steps. Please reply with any corrections and we'll update the MAP.

High-level goal
- Medisprint wants predictable low-latency LLM inference for clinical triage (customer-facing) and internal document summarization (batch). Primary objective: reduce tail latency spikes while keeping inference cost predictable for Q4 ramp.

Pain points called out
- Occasional p95 latency spikes during morning batch window causing delays in downstream processing.
- Data isolation requirement for PHI-adjacent logs — you indicated some workloads must be isolated by tenant and retained on customer-only storage.
- Procurement timeline pressure: procurement team wants procurement-ready SOW and high-level cost anchors within 2 weeks.

Workload profile (from call) — please confirm numbers below
- Production traffic: ~1200 requests/minute peak (burst to 2000 for scheduled jobs)
- Avg request tokens: 120 input / 90 output
- Model mix: majority open Llama-3-70B-quantized; small portion of 1-2 proprietary fine-tuned models (sensitive).
- Expected growth: 3x over 6 months if metrics meet KPIs

Initial qualification: recommended pathways
1) Dedicated isolated pool (Reserved GPUs) — best for strict isolation and predictable SLOs.
   - Pros: fixed throughput, easier SLA guarantees, KMS/HSM integration for keys, on-demand burst lanes.
   - Cons: higher base commit, longer procurement lead time.
2) Shared-hosted with tenancy controls + workload segmentation — lower initial commit and faster time-to-prod, with logical isolation and selective network egress controls.
   - Pros: lower cost of entry, faster onboarding.
   - Cons: weaker isolation guarantees vs. a physical dedicated pool.

Proposed SLA targets to discuss with infra/ops
- Availability: 99.95% for dedicated pool (target)
- Dispatch p95 latency for interactive endpoints: <= 150ms (baseline)
- Batch job throughput SLA: X tokens/sec guarantee (we'll size after you confirm batch window and concurrency)

Immediate next steps (I own first two, Ben will handle technical sizing)
- Lydia: confirm the workload numbers above and flag which workloads must be PHI-isolated (due Tue 5/18).
- Ben: will follow up with an initial sizing and two capacity option sketches (dedicated vs. segmented shared) by Mon 5/17.
- Chloe: draft SOW placeholder and MAP; share workload template (attached) for your infra/engineering team to populate.

Attachments included: Workload_Inputs_Template.xlsx (please fill tab "PeakProfile"), SOW-draft-v0.1.pdf (placeholder)

If helpful I can set up a 60-min tech deep-dive next week with our serving runtime team — propose Wed 5/19 10:00am PT or Thu 5/20 11:00am PT.

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

--
Chloe Martin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

From: Dr. Lydia Cho <lydia@medsprint.io>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, procurement@medsprint.io
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 11:03:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: GPU reservation qualification and proposed pathways

Chloe — thanks for the clean summary. Confirming the numbers with a couple of clarifications:
- Peak stated is accurate but please plan for a 2.5x stress factor on scheduled batch windows (we see very spiky loads).
- The proprietary fine-tuned models (two models) must be in an isolated pool; the rest can run in a segmented shared environment. This is non-negotiable because of our audit controls.
- For compliance: we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and an answer on whether logs containing PHI can be routed to our customer-managed S3 (we discussed earlier).

Procurement note: procurement@medsprint.io asks for a CLARITY SOW (high-level commercial + termination terms) and a ballpark monthly commit for both pathways. Can you provide ballpark commits (monthly $) by EOD Tue 5/18?

Tech deep-dive: Thu 5/20 11:00am PT works for me. Please include someone from your runtime team who can speak to KV-cache behavior and cold-start mitigation.

Best,
Lydia
Dr. Lydia Cho
VP of Product | Medisprint
lydia@medsprint.io

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Dr. Lydia Cho <lydia@medsprint.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: GPU reservation qualification and proposed pathways

Lydia / Chloe — quick technical note ahead of the deep-dive. I sketched two concrete options and a preliminary sizing ask (we'll refine after you populate the workload sheet):

Option A — Physical dedicated pool (Recommended for proprietary models)
- Sizing anchor: for the proprietary models + interactive surface at your reported peak, initial reserved pool of 8xA100-equivalent nodes (supports steady 1200 req/min with headroom for 2.5x burst).
- Isolation: physical tenant siloing, dedicated NVMe for checkpointing, customer-managed KMS support.
- SLA: Availability 99.95%, targeted p95 <= 120-150ms for typical 120-token decodes (fine-tuning may change this).
- Ballpark commit (placeholder): $110k–$140k/month depending on node type and burst policy.

Option B — Segmented shared pool + tenant-level isolation rules (Lower commit)
- Sizing anchor: logical capacity equivalent to 5xA100-equivalent nodes for interactive workloads, batch jobs scheduled with priority lanes.
- Isolation: network egress locks, tenant-aware KV cache; less strict than physical silo.
- SLA: Availability 99.9%, p95 target ~150–220ms depending on complexity.
- Ballpark commit (placeholder): $45k–$70k/month.

Open questions for Lydia before finalizing numbers
- Which models must be in physical isolation vs. logical? Please list model IDs.
- Confirm batch window schedule and concurrency per job (we need the batch job start times and typical duration).
- Any hard token-retention or log-forwarding constraints (e.g., all logs must land in your S3 located in us-west-2)?

I'll bring our runtime lead (Samir) to the Thu 5/20 11:00am PT call; he'll walk through KV cache warm strategies and autoscaling behavior. Chloe — I'll prepare a two-slide cost vs SLA tradeoff and a starter SOW paragraph for procurement.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (628) 555-0199

Attachment: Workload_Inputs_Template.xlsx (updated - added notes on "batch_window")

From: Dr. Lydia Cho <lydia@medsprint.io>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medsprint.io
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 16:39:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: GPU reservation qualification and proposed pathways

Thanks — this is useful and aligns with what procurement expects. Quick replies:
- Models to isolate: ms-ft-neo-01, ms-ft-qa-02 (both flagged as PHI-involved).
- Batch window: daily 05:30–07:30 PT (heavy ingest/transform), typical runtime 30–90 minutes; concurrency peaks ~40 jobs.
- Logs: yes, PHI-adjacent logs must be routed to our customer bucket in us-west-2 and retained 90 days.

Procurement: I'll ask procurement@medsprint.io to review the placeholder commits once you share them Tue EOD. Also they've started a vendor checklist (SOC2) — attaching the doc they referenced. Can someone from Redwood share a SOC2 point-of-contact and a redacted cert?

Confirming Thu 5/20 11:00am PT for the deep-dive — invite to follow. Thank you all.

--
Dr. Lydia Cho
VP of Product | Medisprint
